source.title: From pixels to planning: scale-free active inference (Renormalising Generative Models)

confidence_rationale: Direction convention: 'weakens' = weakens the distinct-novel-object reading. This is the decisive single-formalism entry for capacity (d) AND for the four-capacity combination. The Renormalising Generative Model is one discrete state-space model whose renormalisation-group operator coarse-grains/refines across scale (d), which learns its own structure/compositionality (c), embedded in active inference so it does directed inference + action (a) on a factor-graph-compatible substrate that carries undirected factors (b). One object, all four capacities + offline learning. Held at 0.7: it is a 2024 preprint (not yet a settled peer-reviewed venue at pull time) and the four-capacity unification is read off the construction rather than benchmarked against REE's exact list.
failure_signatures: Preprint, large (multi-section) paper; the 'covers all four capacities' reading is architectural inference, not a benchmark against REE's capacity list.
Contains no residue/non-erasure primitive; the RG operator explicitly DISCARDS 'irrelevant details' at each coarse-graining -- structurally anti-residue, like Bayesian model reduction.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A Renormalising Generative Model (RGM) is a discrete state-space model with a renormalisation-group operator that coarse-grains a description while retaining properties of interest; each level is renormalisable so the model generates and infers causes at any scale, learns compositionality over space and time, and is used for active inference and learning in a dynamic setting.
mapping.ree_translation: DLIF capacity (d) granularity/scale shift -- the sensory -> trajectory -> goal zoom the cluster wants -- is exactly the RG operator. Combined with structure learning (c, Smith 2020 / intrinsic to RGM) and the factor-graph active-inference substrate (a+b+action, de Vries 2017), the RGM is a SINGLE existing object that already jointly delivers the four DLIF capacities the research map called 'the gap is the combination'.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The unification is read off the model's construction, not measured against REE's exact capacity inventory; and the RG operator's coarse-graining DISCARDS detail, so it does not implement residue/non-erasure. Weakens the novelty claim for (a)-(d); does not address residue.
mapping.source_context: Machine-learning preprint; demonstrated on image classification, video/music generation, Atari-like games. No moral/clinical content.

confidence_components.notes: Authoritative author list (Friston + VERSES/active-inference group) but a 2024 preprint at pull time. Mapping fidelity good for capacity (d) and the combination; transfer risk raised because 'scale-free by construction' is an architectural claim demonstrated on perception/games, not on REE's ethical-granularity zoom (note HA4: perceptual coarsening != ethical-precedence selection -- one RG operator may not be the right model for the ethical-constraint scale).
